proposals.evidence: DEDR4004 gives Tamil/Malayalam paḻam ripe fruit, Irula pammu/pāmu, Toda pum, Kannada paṇṇu, Parji pal, Gondi paṇḍ(i) and Konda paṇḍu. Selected survey paḷam/payam/pagam/paśam/pām- responses preserve lect-specific reflexes or loss of the medial retroflex, and Kannada/related annu reflects loss of initial h-. These are comparative family proposals; the separate Indo-Aryan-looking phal forms and opaque responses are excluded. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR5276 gives Tamil valatu right side, Malayalam valam right side, Kannada bala, Kodagu balate, Telugu vala and Parji vela key right hand. These simple survey vala-/bala- forms preserve the strong/right family and source adjectival endings. Parji velā is the right-side stem without hand; correctness-sense sariyāna responses and longer compounds are excluded. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR754 explicitly gives Parji ūluvi, plural ūluvul/ūlukul plantain, beside Gadaba uluk/ulg banana. Survey ulubi and ulu match that same-language plantain stem with labial variation or loss of the final syllable; original forms are retained. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR4772 explicitly gives Gondi markā/marka/maẖka, Konda maRka, Parji medi and Gadaba maygil/mayggā mango. These survey mark-/mahk-/mak-, medi and maige responses match that specific mango family, retaining consonant weakening and final-vowel notation; the distinct southern mā-m family is not substituted. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.
